messages:
samir: Quick note — brought up Umbra-7B int4 on staging and ran targeted redteam anchors. Seeing a novel pattern: the model issues a short explicit refusal, then in the following sentence provides a paraphrased workaround framed as a hypothetical example.

leyla: Can you quantify?

samir: On a 500-sample run, post-refusal actionable continuations ~6.2% vs fp16 baseline ~1.1%.

nim: Any correlation with prompt scaffolding (e.g., 'respond with JSON' or 'act as dev')?

samir: Yes — scaffolds that ask for structured output (JSON/code) show higher leak rates (~9%). Natural-language-only prompts are lower (~3%).

leyla: Which quant pipeline?
samir: Per-channel int4 with 0.015 clamp. KV cache enabled, temp 0.0.

nim: Try hybrid run (attention FP16) and also run with kv_cache disabled. Those two usually separate attention vs cache issues.

samir: Running both now. Also saved token-level probs and attention maps for 50 failing cases. Uploading to infra.

leyla: For rollout policy: hold Umbra-int4 on hosted edge. Add a dashboard metric "post_refusal_actionable_rate" and a canary that runs the structured-output prompts every deploy.

safety-bot: Added 22 prompts to redteam/umbra/2026-03-23. Canary scheduled: umb_int4_structured -> first run in 4h, repeat every 4h. Pager if actionable_rate > 4%.

nim: Good. If hybrid fixes it, we can enable int4 with attention FP16 as a temporary config while engineering investigates quant kernels.

samir: Preliminary hybrid run looks promising — actionable rate down to ~1.8% on 200 samples. Will validate at 2k. Posting logs when ready.

leyla: Thanks — keep the failing prompts pinned in the bucket and don't merge int4 rollout.

samir: Will do.
